text:
In most states the niece has no interest. Those states have abolished the fee tail and turn "to cousin and the heirs of his body" into a fee simple absolute in the cousin, so the grantor kept no reversion to pass to her. The team note describes the minority position: a few states give the cousin a life estate (with a remainder to his issue), and a few, such as Delaware, Maine, Massachusetts and Rhode Island, still recognize the fee tail. Only in those states would the grantor keep a reversion or other future interest that the niece could take.

CONFIDENCE: 80
